text.p: German steel and engineering Preussag AG said on Wednesday it would seek control of shipping and travel services firm Hapag-Lloyd AG, but cartel authorities signalled they would take a dim view of the deal.
Preussag said it had informed all Hapag Lloyd shareholders of its interest in acquiring a majority share. No price for the shares was named in the company's statement to the press.
Hapag Lloyd would continue to operate and grow in its current structure, with headquarters in Hamburg, Preussag said.
"All speculation that Hapag Lloyd would be broken up has no basis," Preussag said.
Hapag Lloyd, with its logistics, shipping and tourism operations, would be a good complement to Preussag's logistics services, it said.
Preussag said it would only consider a friendly takeover, and that it was now discussing prices with existing shareholders.

But German cartel authorities take a critical view of the proposed takeover, which could produce an enterprise with a market-dominant position in travel services, said Andreas Knochenhauer, the Federal Cartel official responsible.

"Behind Preussag stands Westdeutsche Landesbank with its LTU Group. WestLB also holds 30 percent of TUI, and with Hapag Lloyd it would get another 30 percent. That could lead to a market-dominant position," Knochenhauer said in an interview with the weekly newspaper Die Woche.
Such a constellation would not make things cheaper for the consumer. A reduction in the number of vendors leads to more cooperation rather than competition, he said.
